subject.title: [Bug]: codex harness mirrored-session-history read fails for ephemeral sessions and on failover; one-shot cleanup retires shared app-server client while turns are in flight

question: Should Codex one-shot runs use isolated or lease-safe clients, and what transcript source should be canonical for fallback when the Codex mirror is missing or unsupported?
rationale: The remaining work crosses Codex app-server lifecycle ownership and cross-provider failover semantics, where automation should not choose between compatibility, replay safety, and user-visible recovery without maintainer intent.

options.title: Use isolated or lease-safe one-shot clients
options.body: Make active-memory and other one-shot Codex runs unable to retire a shared client that can affect user turns, then feed fallback from canonical OpenClaw transcript state when safe.

options.title: Keep retirement with stronger guards
options.body: Retain shared-client retirement after one-shot cleanup only if active-lease/refcount tests and live proof show active user turns cannot be closed, stranded, or replayed without context.

options.title: Fail visibly instead of cross-provider replay
options.body: If safe transcript continuity is not supported, stop fallback from answering without context and surface a recoverable user-facing error for this failure class.

recommendation.title: Use isolated or lease-safe one-shot clients
recommendation.body: Make active-memory and other one-shot Codex runs unable to retire a shared client that can affect user turns, then feed fallback from canonical OpenClaw transcript state when safe.

likelyOwner.reason: They carried the recent partial mirrored-history fix and are the closest recent contributor to the current Codex session-history repair path.
